title: Integrated Fish Farming
source_note: Grounded in standard aquaculture/fisheries curricula (NUC-aligned) covering integrated agriculture-aquaculture (IAA) systems: fish-livestock, fish-crop (rice-fish), fish-poultry integration, pond fertilization with manure, nutrient cycling, waste utilization, polyculture, and economics of integrated systems.

questions.question: What is the primary principle behind integrated fish farming?
options: Using by-products or wastes from one farming enterprise as inputs for fish production, and vice versa
Growing only one species of fish in isolation
Farming fish exclusively in cages in open water
Importing all fish feed from external commercial sources
questions.correct_answer: Using by-products or wastes from one farming enterprise as inputs for fish production, and vice versa
questions.explanation: Integrated fish farming links aquaculture with crop or livestock production so that wastes/by-products from one system serve as inputs (e.g., fertilizer, feed) for the other, improving overall resource efficiency.

questions.question: In a fish-cum-poultry (fish-duck or fish-chicken) integrated system, what is the main benefit to the pond?
options: Poultry droppings fall or are washed into the pond and fertilize it, boosting natural fish food (plankton) production
Poultry droppings poison the water and must be filtered out completely
The poultry house replaces the need for a pond altogether
Poultry feathers are used directly as fish feed pellets
questions.correct_answer: Poultry droppings fall or are washed into the pond and fertilize it, boosting natural fish food (plankton) production
questions.explanation: Poultry manure enriches pond water with nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus), stimulating phytoplankton and zooplankton growth that fish feed on, reducing the need for supplementary feed.

questions.question: Which livestock is most commonly integrated with fish ponds in the fish-cum-pig system?
options: Pigs, whose sty is built over or beside the pond so manure/wastewater drains into it
Camels
Horses
Sheep only, never pigs
questions.correct_answer: Pigs, whose sty is built over or beside the pond so manure/wastewater drains into it
questions.explanation: The fish-cum-pig system is a classic IAA model where pig manure and washings fertilize the pond, and pigs may also be fed some pond by-products.

questions.question: What is 'rice-fish culture'?
options: Simultaneous or rotational rearing of fish within rice paddies, using the flooded field as both crop and fish habitat
Growing rice using fish oil as fertilizer only
A method of drying rice using fish smoking racks
Feeding rice husks exclusively to marine fish
questions.correct_answer: Simultaneous or rotational rearing of fish within rice paddies, using the flooded field as both crop and fish habitat
questions.explanation: Rice-fish culture uses the same flooded field to produce both rice and fish, with fish helping control pests/weeds and their waste fertilizing the rice.

questions.question: In an integrated fish-cum-crop system, what ecological service do fish typically provide to the crop?
options: Controlling insect pests and weeds while their excreta fertilize the crop
Pollinating the crop flowers directly
Replacing the need for irrigation water entirely
Producing oxygen for photosynthesis above the water surface
questions.correct_answer: Controlling insect pests and weeds while their excreta fertilize the crop
questions.explanation: Fish in rice-fish or vegetable-fish systems feed on pests, larvae, and weeds, and their waste adds nutrients, reducing the need for pesticides and chemical fertilizer.

questions.question: Why is organic manure (e.g., poultry, pig, or cattle dung) applied to fish ponds in integrated systems?
options: To decompose and release nutrients that stimulate plankton growth as natural fish food
To directly poison unwanted predator fish
To increase the salinity of freshwater ponds
To harden the pond bottom against erosion
questions.correct_answer: To decompose and release nutrients that stimulate plankton growth as natural fish food
questions.explanation: Organic manure decomposes in water, releasing nitrogen and phosphorus that fuel phytoplankton and zooplankton blooms, the base of the pond food web supporting fish growth.

questions.question: What is a major risk of over-fertilizing a fish pond with animal manure?
options: Oxygen depletion from excessive organic decomposition, leading to fish kills
The pond water becomes too clear for fish to see food
Fish grow abnormally large fins
The pond permanently loses its ability to hold water
questions.correct_answer: Oxygen depletion from excessive organic decomposition, leading to fish kills
questions.explanation: Excess manure causes high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) as bacteria decompose it, depleting dissolved oxygen and potentially causing fish mortality, especially at night.

questions.question: Which fish species is most suited to polyculture in integrated systems because it feeds low in the food chain on plankton and detritus?
options: Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
Great white shark
Piranha
Barracuda
questions.correct_answer: Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
questions.explanation: Tilapia are omnivorous, feeding on plankton, detritus, and periphyton, making them ideal for integrated and manure-fertilized pond systems in Nigeria.

questions.question: What does 'polyculture' mean in the context of integrated fish farming?
options: Stocking multiple fish species with complementary feeding niches in the same pond
Growing fish in multiple separate countries
Using multiple pond liners for one species
Breeding only hybrid catfish species
questions.correct_answer: Stocking multiple fish species with complementary feeding niches in the same pond
questions.explanation: Polyculture combines species that occupy different feeding niches (e.g., surface feeders, bottom feeders, plankton feeders) to maximize use of natural pond food and space.

questions.question: In a fish-cum-cattle integrated system, what role does the pond often play for the cattle?
options: A water source and the manure collection point that fertilizes the pond in return
The sole source of cattle feed protein
A breeding ground exclusively for cattle
A replacement for cattle grazing land
questions.correct_answer: A water source and the manure collection point that fertilizes the pond in return
questions.explanation: Cattle often drink from or are washed near the pond, and their dung is collected and applied to the pond as organic fertilizer, closing the nutrient loop.

questions.question: What is the recommended approach to introducing manure into a fish pond to avoid sudden oxygen crashes?
options: Apply manure gradually and in moderate, regular doses rather than one large dose
Dump the entire season's manure supply in a single application
Apply manure only during a full moon
Never apply manure and rely solely on commercial feed
questions.correct_answer: Apply manure gradually and in moderate, regular doses rather than one large dose
questions.explanation: Gradual, regular manure application prevents overloading the pond with organic matter that could deplete oxygen abruptly, maintaining stable water quality.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the economic advantage of integrated fish farming for smallholder farmers?
options: It reduces production costs by recycling farm wastes and diversifies income from multiple products
It eliminates the need for any farm labor
It guarantees higher fish prices than monoculture
It requires no capital investment whatsoever
questions.correct_answer: It reduces production costs by recycling farm wastes and diversifies income from multiple products
questions.explanation: By recycling on-farm wastes (feed cost savings) and producing both crops/livestock and fish, integrated systems lower input costs and spread income risk across products.

questions.question: What is the significance of dissolved oxygen monitoring in manured (fertilized) integrated fish ponds, especially at dawn?
options: Dissolved oxygen is typically lowest at dawn after a night of respiration without photosynthesis, risking fish stress or death
Dissolved oxygen is always highest at dawn regardless of conditions
Dawn monitoring is irrelevant since oxygen levels never change
Oxygen levels only matter during midday feeding
questions.correct_answer: Dissolved oxygen is typically lowest at dawn after a night of respiration without photosynthesis, risking fish stress or death
questions.explanation: At night, phytoplankton respire (consuming oxygen) without photosynthesizing, so oxygen is depleted through the night and reaches its lowest point just before sunrise.

questions.question: Which crop is most classically associated with integrated aquaculture in Asian and adapted African systems due to its flooded cultivation?
options: Rice
Maize
Cassava
Yam
questions.correct_answer: Rice
questions.explanation: Rice is grown in flooded paddies, providing a natural shared habitat with fish, making rice-fish culture the most established form of fish-crop integration.

questions.question: What is a 'vegetable-cum-fish' (dike-cropping) system?
options: Growing vegetables on pond dikes/embankments while fish are cultured in the pond, using pond mud as fertilizer for the vegetables
Growing vegetables inside the fish pond water
Feeding vegetables directly to filter-feeding fish
Using vegetable oil to control pond algae
questions.correct_answer: Growing vegetables on pond dikes/embankments while fish are cultured in the pond, using pond mud as fertilizer for the vegetables
questions.explanation: Pond dike-cropping uses the raised banks around fish ponds to grow vegetables, benefiting from nutrient-rich pond sediment while fish are reared in the water below.

questions.question: Why is African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) often included in integrated systems alongside tilapia?
options: It is a carnivorous/omnivorous bottom feeder that helps control tilapia overpopulation by preying on excess fry
It only eats commercial pellets and nothing else
It cannot survive in ponds with any organic matter
It requires marine (saltwater) conditions
questions.correct_answer: It is a carnivorous/omnivorous bottom feeder that helps control tilapia overpopulation by preying on excess fry
questions.explanation: Clarias is often stocked with tilapia to prey on excess tilapia fry, preventing overcrowding and stunted growth, a common polyculture management strategy.

questions.question: What is the main function of a 'compost pit' or 'manure crib' positioned at the pond edge in integrated systems?
options: To allow controlled leaching of nutrients from decomposing manure into the pond water
To store fish harvested from the pond
To breed mosquitoes for fish feed
To filter pond water before it reaches crops
questions.correct_answer: To allow controlled leaching of nutrients from decomposing manure into the pond water
questions.explanation: A manure crib or compost pit at the pond edge lets rain and seepage gradually wash nutrients into the pond, providing a steady, controlled fertilization source.

questions.question: In integrated fish-livestock systems, what stocking density consideration is critical compared to fish-only monoculture ponds?
options: Lower fish stocking density may be needed if natural food from manure is the primary feed source, to avoid overcrowding beyond the pond's carrying capacity
Stocking density is irrelevant in integrated systems
Fish must always be stocked at the same density as pure monoculture, regardless of feed source
Only fingerlings under 1 gram can be stocked in integrated ponds
questions.correct_answer: Lower fish stocking density may be needed if natural food from manure is the primary feed source, to avoid overcrowding beyond the pond's carrying capacity
questions.explanation: Since natural food production from manure is limited, stocking density must match the pond's natural carrying capacity unless supplemental feed is also given.

questions.question: What water quality parameter is most directly increased by excessive manure loading, potentially becoming toxic to fish?
options: Ammonia (un-ionized NH3)
Dissolved calcium carbonate only
Water hardness exclusively
Barometric pressure
questions.correct_answer: Ammonia (un-ionized NH3)
questions.explanation: Manure decomposition releases nitrogenous waste; excess organic loading raises ammonia levels, which is toxic to fish especially at high pH and temperature.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a fish-cum-agriculture waste recycling loop?
options: Using pond sediment (sludge) rich in nutrients as fertilizer for adjacent crop fields
Burning pond sludge to generate electricity for the farm
Exporting all pond sludge off the farm to avoid reuse
Using only chemical fertilizer and never pond sludge
questions.correct_answer: Using pond sediment (sludge) rich in nutrients as fertilizer for adjacent crop fields
questions.explanation: Nutrient-rich pond sludge, periodically removed during pond desilting, is a valuable organic fertilizer for surrounding crops, closing the farm nutrient cycle.

questions.question: Which factor most limits how much livestock manure a given pond can safely absorb per unit area?
options: The pond's assimilative capacity, determined by water depth, temperature, aeration, and existing organic load
The number of fish species stocked, regardless of pond size
The color of the pond dike soil
The distance of the pond from the nearest market
questions.correct_answer: The pond's assimilative capacity, determined by water depth, temperature, aeration, and existing organic load
questions.explanation: A pond's ability to process organic waste depends on physical and biological factors like depth, temperature (affecting decomposition rate), and oxygen availability.

questions.question: In azolla-fish integration, what role does the aquatic fern Azolla play?
options: It fixes nitrogen (via symbiotic cyanobacteria) and serves as a nutrient-rich supplementary feed for fish
It is a toxic weed that must be eradicated from fish ponds
It replaces the need for a pond dike
It is used only as a pond liner material
questions.correct_answer: It fixes nitrogen (via symbiotic cyanobacteria) and serves as a nutrient-rich supplementary feed for fish
questions.explanation: Azolla hosts nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria (Anabaena azollae) and is a protein-rich floating plant that can be harvested as feed for fish and livestock in integrated systems.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of periodic liming in integrated fish ponds that receive heavy organic (manure) loading?
options: To neutralize acidity, improve water quality, and reduce pathogen load from organic buildup
To increase fish reproduction speed directly
To replace the need for water exchange permanently
To dye the pond water a lighter color for aesthetics
questions.correct_answer: To neutralize acidity, improve water quality, and reduce pathogen load from organic buildup
questions.explanation: Lime raises pH, precipitates some nutrients, helps control pathogens/parasites, and counteracts acidification from organic matter decomposition.

questions.question: Which combination best represents a 'triple integration' system in tropical fish farming?
options: Fish-livestock (e.g., pig)-crop (e.g., vegetable on dikes) combined on the same farm unit
Fish reared with no other component at all
Two separate fish ponds with no other enterprise
Fish combined only with fish processing equipment
questions.correct_answer: Fish-livestock (e.g., pig)-crop (e.g., vegetable on dikes) combined on the same farm unit
questions.explanation: Triple (or multiple) integration links fish, livestock, and crop production in one farm system so wastes and by-products cycle between all three components.

questions.question: What is a key disease-transmission risk that must be managed in fish-livestock integrated systems?
options: Zoonotic or cross-contamination risk from untreated animal waste entering ponds used for food fish
Fish transmitting avian influenza directly to poultry
Livestock developing gill diseases from pond water
There is no disease risk in any integrated system
questions.correct_answer: Zoonotic or cross-contamination risk from untreated animal waste entering ponds used for food fish
questions.explanation: Raw manure can carry pathogens; proper composting or controlled application is needed to reduce microbial contamination risks to farmed fish intended for human consumption.

questions.question: Which fish feeding guild benefits most directly from phytoplankton blooms stimulated by manure in integrated ponds?
options: Filter/plankton feeders such as tilapia and silver carp
Strict piscivores that eat only other fish
Fish that feed exclusively on floating commercial pellets
Fish that only eat insects above the water surface
questions.correct_answer: Filter/plankton feeders such as tilapia and silver carp
questions.explanation: Plankton-feeding species directly exploit the phytoplankton and zooplankton blooms produced from decomposed manure, making them ideal for fertilized pond systems.

questions.question: What is the recommended practice regarding fresh (uncomposted) manure application directly into ponds stocking table-size fish near harvest?
options: It should be avoided or minimized to reduce risk of off-flavor, pathogen contamination, and oxygen depletion close to harvest
It should be doubled to speed up final growth
It has no effect on fish quality near harvest
It should replace all commercial feed right before harvest
questions.correct_answer: It should be avoided or minimized to reduce risk of off-flavor, pathogen contamination, and oxygen depletion close to harvest
questions.explanation: Heavy fresh manure loading near harvest risks off-flavors from algal blooms, pathogen contamination, and dangerous oxygen depletion, so it is reduced as harvest approaches.

questions.question: In a fish-cum-duck system, why are ducks particularly well suited compared to some other poultry?
options: Ducks can swim on the pond directly, depositing manure straight into the water and also foraging on some aquatic organisms
Ducks cannot tolerate any proximity to water
Ducks require no feed at all when kept near ponds
Ducks eliminate the need for fish stocking entirely
questions.correct_answer: Ducks can swim on the pond directly, depositing manure straight into the water and also foraging on some aquatic organisms
questions.explanation: Unlike chickens, ducks are aquatic birds that swim on the pond, directly fertilizing it with droppings while also feeding on some pond organisms like snails and insects.

questions.question: What does the term 'carrying capacity' mean in the context of an integrated fish pond?
options: The maximum fish biomass a pond can sustain given its natural food, oxygen, and waste-assimilation limits
The maximum weight of manure a farmer can physically carry to the pond
The number of years a pond can be used before it must be abandoned
The volume of water a pond can hold in liters
questions.correct_answer: The maximum fish biomass a pond can sustain given its natural food, oxygen, and waste-assimilation limits
questions.explanation: Carrying capacity refers to the upper limit of fish biomass a pond ecosystem can support sustainably based on its natural resources and waste-processing ability.

questions.question: Which economic principle explains why integrated fish farming can be more profitable per unit land than separate monoculture enterprises?
options: It captures synergies that reduce input costs (e.g., feed, fertilizer) while producing multiple marketable outputs from the same land and labor base
It always eliminates market risk completely
It guarantees government subsidy eligibility
It removes the need for any record-keeping
questions.correct_answer: It captures synergies that reduce input costs (e.g., feed, fertilizer) while producing multiple marketable outputs from the same land and labor base
questions.explanation: Integration reduces costs through waste recycling (less purchased feed/fertilizer) and diversifies income streams, improving overall farm profitability and land-use efficiency.

questions.question: What monitoring practice helps a farmer decide when to reduce or stop manure application to an integrated pond?
options: Regularly checking water transparency (Secchi disc), dissolved oxygen, and fish behavior for signs of stress or excessive turbidity
Counting the number of birds visiting the pond daily
Measuring only the pond's surface area once at construction
Checking the market price of fish feed alone
questions.correct_answer: Regularly checking water transparency (Secchi disc), dissolved oxygen, and fish behavior for signs of stress or excessive turbidity
questions.explanation: Secchi disc readings indicate plankton density/turbidity, and combined with dissolved oxygen and fish behavior monitoring, guide farmers on adjusting fertilization rates.
